title: Graded square-zero lifting for a smooth affine algebra
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $C=\bigoplus_{n\in\mathbf Z}C_n$ a commutative unital $R$-algebra with an integer grading: each $C_n$ is an $R$-submodule, every element has a unique finite homogeneous expansion, $1\in C_0$, the image of $R$ lies in $C_0$, and $C_nC_m\subseteq C_{n+m}$. Suppose $\operatorname{Spec}C\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is smooth [def-weil-affine-spectrum] [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] and $C$ is finitely presented over $R$, meaning it is a quotient of a polynomial ring in finitely many variables by a finitely generated ideal. Let $D=\bigoplus_{n\in\mathbf Z}D_n$ be any commutative unital graded $R$-algebra in the same sense. Let $J\subseteq D$ be a homogeneous square-zero ideal: $J=\bigoplus_n(J\cap D_n)$ and $xy=0$ for all $x,y\in J$. Give $D/J$ the quotient grading. Every degree-preserving $R$-algebra homomorphism $h:C\to D/J$ admits a degree-preserving $R$-algebra homomorphism $\widetilde h:C\to D$ with $q\widetilde h=h$, where $q:D\to D/J$ is the quotient homomorphism. Neither $R$ nor $D$ is required to be Noetherian, reduced, or nonzero, and neither grading is required to have only nonnegative degrees.

source.place: Tags 00TI (definition-formally-smooth) and 00TN (proposition-smooth-formally-smooth), graded refinement written by the agent, not a statement asserted verbatim by Stacks. This is the equivariant infinitesimal ingredient for Conrad, Theorem 4.1.7(4), proof pp.113-114.

proof.text: Forget the gradings temporarily. By [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], the given smooth morphism $\operatorname{Spec}C\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is formally smooth. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-affine-formally-smooth-iff-ring-lifting] with $S=C$, $D=D$, $N=J$ and $g=h$. Its hypotheses hold since $D$ is a commutative $R$-algebra and $J^2=0$. Obtain an ordinary $R$-algebra homomorphism $f:C\to D$ with $qf=h$. No grading condition is asserted for $f$.

Let $\pi_i:D\to D_i\subset D$ be homogeneous projection. The direct-sum decomposition into $R$-submodules makes each $\pi_i$ $R$-linear. Because $J$ is homogeneous, $q$ commutes with homogeneous projections: decompose any element into its finitely many homogeneous components and apply $q$, using uniqueness of the quotient grading. For $x\in C_n$ write $f(x)=\sum_i f(x)_i$. Since $qf(x)=h(x)$ has degree $n$, we have $f(x)_i\in J$ for $i\ne n$ and $q(f(x)_n)=h(x)$. Define $\widetilde h(\sum_n x_n)=\sum_n\pi_n(f(x_n))$. These finite sums define an $R$-linear map, since each restricted map $\pi_n f|_{C_n}$ is $R$-linear and homogeneous expansions are unique. It preserves degrees and satisfies $q\widetilde h=h$. Moreover $1$ and the image of $R$ have degree zero and $f$ fixes them, so $\widetilde h(1)=1$ and $\widetilde h(r)=r$ for $r\in R$.

source.place: Tag 00TI (definition-formally-smooth); homogeneous-component refinement written by Q129.

proof.text: For $x\in C_n$ and $y\in C_m$, use multiplicativity of $f$ and take degree $n+m$: $\widetilde h(xy)=\pi_{n+m}(f(x)f(y))=\sum_{i+j=n+m}f(x)_i f(y)_j$. The sum is finite. The pair $(i,j)=(n,m)$ contributes $\widetilde h(x)\widetilde h(y)$. For every other pair, cancellation in $\mathbf Z$ implies both $i\ne n$ and $j\ne m$, so both factors belong to $J$ by step 2 and their product is zero. Therefore $\widetilde h(xy)=\widetilde h(x)\widetilde h(y)$ on homogeneous elements. For arbitrary finite expansions $x=\sum_n x_n$ and $y=\sum_m y_m$, distribute their product and use the $R$-linearity from step 2 to get the same identity. Thus $\widetilde h$ is the required graded unital $R$-algebra lift.
